title: Passive mechanical loading does not reproduce Anthrobot-induced neural repair

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Passive mechanical loading does not reproduce Anthrobot-induced neural repair

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Placing a piece of agarose on neuronal scratches for 4 days to provide passive mechanical loading induces no repair, indicating that simple mechanical contact is not sufficient for the gap closure seen with Anthrobot superbots.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Anthrobots Can Promote Gap Closures on Scratched Live Neuronal Monolayer Tissues

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Finally, in order to test whether simple (passive) mechanical contact was sufficient to induce the same effect, we incubated neuronal scratches for 4 days with a piece of agarose on top to provide mechanical loading; this induced no repair (see Figure S11, Supporting Information).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Gumuskaya G, Srivastava P, Cooper BG, Lesser H, Semegran B, Garnier S, Levin M, “Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells”, Advanced science (Weinheim, Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany) (2024), doi:10.1002/advs.202303575; section “Results › Anthrobots Can Promote Gap Closures on Scratched Live Neuronal Monolayer Tissues”. Scope: Scratched hiNSC-derived human neuronal monolayers in vitro

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2024-anthrobots-22: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.64

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The negative agarose outcome is readily measurable from existing supporting material. It rules out one passive object but not simple mechanical contact in general, so only the narrow control claim is resolvable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure gap closure after four days under agarose and compare it with untreated scratches and superbots across matched sizes, loads, and contact areas.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Agarose may not match superbot geometry, compliance, adhesion, or dynamic forces.

Replicate numbers and raw control images may be sparse.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.32
discriminating power: 0.52
data existence: 0.56
analysis feasibility: 0.9
operationalizability: 0.96

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Gap closure under agarose versus under a living bridge is a direct negative-control contrast. The paper reports no repair and does not release the images or densities. One unmatched passive load is also a limited rival to contact mechanics, and neither the null result nor a better-matched control can be checked from open files.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Incubate matched neuronal scratches for four days under agarose pieces sized like superbots and measure gap closure against superbot bridges and against empty scratches. No repair under agarose, with repair under bridges, would support the claim that passive mechanical loading is insufficient; closure under agarose would refute that negative result.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Agarose stiffness, chemistry and contact area need not match a living bridge.

The agarose control is a supporting figure, not a deposited coverage table.

A single passive material does not exhaust mechanical explanations.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

data adequacy: 0.12
operationalizability: 0.88
discriminating power: 0.42
analysis feasibility: 0.16
